title: Sylvan Financial POC econ & benchmark scoping
summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics for transaction-classification assistant; discussed target QPS, latency SLOs, per-token budgeting, caching strategies and an initial benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run 2-tier benchmark, share pricing spreadsheet, and sync on SOC2/arch docs.
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send detailed pricing spreadsheet with per-model estimates and example batch configs - due 2026-12-04
Maya Kapoor - Propose benchmark harness and initial test prompts; include 95th/99th latency collectors - due 2026-12-08
Carlos Mendes - Provide sample workload trace (QPS + typical prompt length distribution) - due 2026-12-06
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-tier benchmark (Hosted small-run + Dedicated baseline) and share results
Customer to provision test data and a short anonymized trace file
Schedule deep-dive to review benchmark results and finalize POC acceptance criteria (tentative week of 2026-12-14)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Sylvan Head of ML), Aisha Noor (Sylvan Platform Eng), Tom Beckett (Sylvan CTO)

Summary note: casual, SE-heavy scoping, some audio dropouts at ~00:22.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for making the time. i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account and with me is Maya, our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: hey Jordan, Carlos here.
[00:12] Aisha Noor: Aisha here.
[00:14] Tom Beckett: Tom on the line.
[00:16] Maya Kapoor: hi all.

[00:25] Jordan Lee: i'll give a 2 minute context on what we heard in the email — Sylvan's building a transaction classification assistant that needs to run at low latency for customer-facing flows, goal is to do a proof of concept to validate unit economics and latency tiers. want to confirm success criteria and the workload shape.

[00:45] Carlos Mendes: yeah exactly. we have two primary flows: a quick inline classification (avg prompt + history ~120 tokens, want 95th < 150ms ideally) and an async batch reconciliation job (large context 2k-6k tokens, throughput focused). qps for inline is variable, peak around 60 qps sustained for short bursts, steady state 12-18 qps.

[01:20] Maya Kapoor: cool. two flow pattern maps well to Redwood's routing: latency-first small model variant for inline, and throughput-optimized variant for reconciliation. question for you — what's your budget envelope for the POC and the expected run cadence?

[01:36] Tom Beckett: budget is constrained. C-level is giving us a runway of roughly 10k USD for the POC (one month equivalent). If we can show per-op economics and a clear path to under our current infra spend, we'd expand.

[01:55] Jordan Lee: understood. that's tight but workable for targeted benchmarks. we'll focus the POC on demonstrating per-token cost model and the impact of batching and KV/prefix caching on per-inference cost.

[02:10] Aisha Noor: detail on data residency / security — we need SOC2 plus audit logs, SSO integration. we may prefer Redwood Private later but for the POC hosted is fine if audit logs are retained and we can sign an NDA.

[02:30] Maya Kapoor: noted, we have SOC2 docs and a short SOC2 evidence pack. i'll attach the link after the call. for the POC we'll keep logs for 30 days and provide RBAC controls per token.

[02:45] Carlos Mendes: great. can you walk through how you'd estimate per-token costs? we've got weird tokenization on our domain specific texts and variable avg lengths.

[03:00] Maya Kapoor: sure. rough approach: we model two main buckets — small inline model at 3-4B equiv, and a larger 30-70B family for the reconciliation. per-token cost is a function of model latency per token on the chosen hardware, plus infra amortized cost, and then savings from batching and prefix/kvcache reuse. we run a microbenchmark to map tokens-per-second for your trace.

[03:28] Tom Beckett: when you say '3-4B equiv' do you mean quantized variants? we are sensitive to quality; if we drop too low we lose classification accuracy.

[03:38] Maya Kapoor: yes, we propose evals on a small dev set to set the floor. the POC will include accuracy regression thresholds: e.g., <=1% drop in F1 relative to your current model. i'll record that as a success metric.

[03:55] Jordan Lee: can we list explicit acceptance criteria now?
[03:58] Carlos Mendes: let's — success if: 1) inline 95th < 150ms, 2) per-op cost for inline < $0.004 (that's our target), 3) reconciliation throughput of at least 400 tokens/sec per GPU node at 90% utilization, and 4) accuracy within 1% F1.

[04:25] Maya Kapoor: good set. we'll size tests to prove those. a note on the per-op cost: that $0.004 number depends heavily on batching — at low qps batching is limited so we model 3 scenarios: cold (no batching), warm (2-4 req batch window), and optimized (where we can do multi-request batching).

[04:50] Aisha Noor: how do you handle prefix caching / KV cache for the inline flow? we have a lot of repeated prompts and a moderate session window.

[05:02] Maya Kapoor: Redwood supports prefix cache at the request routing layer — we can keep KV caches hot for sessions, which for typical customer sessions yields 30-60% token reduction on average. for POC we'll instrument to show effective token savings and the hit rates.

[05:22] Jordan Lee: also we'll show how autoscaling and burst capacity affects cost — Dedicated pools vs hosted fallbacks. since you're okay with hosted for POC, we'll run a dedicated-like baseline and hosted run to compare.

[05:40] Tom Beckett: any gotchas on latency when caching is used?
[05:44] Maya Kapoor: caching helps latency for repeated prefixes because it avoids recomputing KV state for earlier tokens; resolution time for cache hits is sub-ms extra routing overhead. misses still pay full cost. we'll show 95/99th breakdown.

[06:05] Carlos Mendes: for the reconciliation job — we typically hit 4k token inputs at midnight and need to finish processing within a 2 hour window. we want cost per 1k tokens < $0.02 ideally.

[06:20] Maya Kapoor: that sets a batching-friendly workload. reconciliation is where quantized larger models and larger batch sizes shine. we'll plan a throughput benchmark on a 8-GPU pod to measure tokens/sec and cost.

[06:33] Jordan Lee: let's map deliverables and timeline in the call: immediate deliverables are 1) pricing spreadsheet with per-model per-token estimates, 2) benchmark harness and planned tests, 3) security docs. estimated timing: spreadsheet next business day, harness plan ~4 business days, benchmarks run week after harness sign-off. does that align?

[07:00] Tom Beckett: yes but we need the benchmarks within two weeks to show C-suite. tight margin.

[07:06] Jordan Lee: we can compress — spreadsheet today, harness by Friday, run a quick 24-hour hosted benchmark early next week and a Dedicated baseline mid-next week.

[07:18] Aisha Noor: on the pricing spreadsheet — please include alternate sims for batching windows of 10ms/50ms/200ms, and effects of cache hit rates 0/25/50/75%. that's the sensitivity checklist we'll use.

[07:34] Maya Kapoor: got it, we'll model those permutations. we'll also provide a knobs table — min batch size, max latency window, kv cache ttl, and quantization profile.

[07:48] Carlos Mendes: curious: what hardware will you use for the Dedicated baseline?

[07:52] Maya Kapoor: for the Dedicated baseline we'll use A100-equivalent nodes for the 30-70B modeling, and 80GB A100 or H100 depending on availability. for the inline we may use 40GB nodes with optimized kernels. we'll include the exact instance SKUs in the spreadsheet. note: H100 gives better throughput but higher cost; we'll show cost/throughput tradeoffs.

[08:20] Tom Beckett: i want to make sure the math is clear in the spreadsheet — show us per-token compute cost, infra amortization, and add-on platform fees.

[08:30] Jordan Lee: yes we'll break down: compute (GPU-hours), infra (network, storage), platform fee (per-request or per-token markup), and any storage egress. example row will show token counts, batch sizes, observed tokens/sec, and resulting per-op $ estimate.

[08:50] Carlos Mendes: any chance you can show a worst-case scenario where burst qps spikes to 150 for 30s? we need to know fallback behavior/cost.

[08:59] Maya Kapoor: we'll include an autoscaling simulation and a fallback policy: if Dedicated capacity is saturated, requests route to hosted lower-tier variants subject to policy. cost for burst routing will be in the spreadsheet and included in the risk section.

[09:20] Jordan Lee: a quick aside — are there any internal guardrails at Sylvan about using third-party hosted inference for customer PII?
[09:29] Aisha Noor: PII is allowed in hosted for test data if anonymized; production will likely have to go Private in our VPC, but POC is fine. we'll provide anonymized sample traces.

[09:40] Maya Kapoor: perfect. that'll help us run realistic tokenization and hit-rate sims.

[09:50] Carlos Mendes: we also want latency percentiles per route. 95th is our primary SLO but 99th matters for small fraction spikes.

[09:59] Maya Kapoor: we'll collect 50/95/99 and tail latencies, plus CPU/GPU utilization. benchmark artifacts will include raw traces and aggregated dashboards.

[10:15] Tom Beckett: can you detail the eval process for accuracy? we need repeatable metrics.

[10:21] Maya Kapoor: yes — we will take your dev test set, run current baseline model and candidate variants, compare precision/recall/F1, and set a pass/fail threshold. we recommend automated regression alerts if later model changes deviate more than 1%.

[10:38] Jordan Lee: any blockers from your side to share the sample traces and dev eval set?
[10:42] Carlos Mendes: we'll sanitize PII and share later today. expect a 5k-line sample of real traffic plus a 1k-example labeled eval set.

[10:52] Maya Kapoor: perfect. for the benchmark harness we'll need a short script to replay the trace and a small adapter to translate your domain text into Redwood request format. we can provide a reference client.

[11:06] Jordan Lee: pricing model note: per-token rates are dynamic but for POC we'll lock to the quoted rates in the spreadsheet so you can compare apples-to-apples.

[11:18] Aisha Noor: what about logging retention — 30 days is fine, but can we flag specific requests for longer retention if needed for debugging?

[11:26] Maya Kapoor: yes, we can set retention rules and export flagged items to your S3 or secure bucket. that's part of the SOC2 evidence pack workflow.

[11:35] Carlos Mendes: anything else on governance? SSO integration details?

[11:39] Jordan Lee: we'll share an SSO/SAML integration guide; POC won't need SSO but the docs will show time-to-prod for Private.

[11:50] Tom Beckett: let's talk timelines quick. if we get sample data by EOD tomorrow can you commit to benchmarks by Dec 10?
[11:58] Jordan Lee: yes — timeline proposed: sample data by 2026-12-03, spreadsheet by 2026-12-04, harness plan by 2026-12-08, hosted quick benchmark 2026-12-09 to 2026-12-10, Dedicated baseline 2026-12-11 to 2026-12-12, review week of 2026-12-14.

[12:22] Aisha Noor: fine. please also include the permutations we discussed (batch windows and cache hit rate sims).

[12:33] Maya Kapoor: we'll provide a sensitivity matrix. also note on model variants: we recommend 3 candidate families — compact (3-4B), mid (13-20B quantized), and large (40-70B) for reconciliation. each will have expected latency and quality bullets.

[12:55] Carlos Mendes: ok great. one last question — do you charge per-embedding or per-token for metadata retrieval?

[13:02] Jordan Lee: retrieval/embedding ops are billed separately; we'll annotate which tests include embeddings. for the inline flow most ops are pure text gen/classification so token billing drives the cost.

[13:18] Tom Beckett: thanks. i want to see a row that shows token savings from prefix caching at 50% hit — that might make the per-op cost look very different.

[13:28] Maya Kapoor: will include that in the sims.

[13:34] Jordan Lee: ok let's recap next steps verbally: Jordan to send pricing spreadsheet and SOC2 link, Maya to deliver harness plan and proposed test prompts, Sylvan to send sanitized sample traces and labeled eval set, then schedule deep-dive week of Dec 14. any other items?

[13:52] Carlos Mendes: no, that covers it.

[13:55] Aisha Noor: quick logistic — please cc legal on the SOC2/NDA attachments.

[14:00] Jordan Lee: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.

[14:06] (small audio dropout)
[14:12] Tom Beckett: thanks all bye.

End of call.
